neighbourhoods.name: Burscough

neighbourhoods.name: Tarleton and Hesketh Bank

neighbourhoods.name: Parbold and Appley Bridge

housing: West Lancashire mixes the market town of Ormskirk, the 1960s new town of Skelmersdale and a large area of flat farmland and villages. Edge Hill University makes student lets common in Ormskirk, while Skelmersdale has many former development corporation homes, some now let privately. Burscough and the villages have seen new estates, and the rural north has farm cottages and bungalows. Most households own their home.
checkinTips: Student houses in Ormskirk near Edge Hill University: record each bedroom's lock, furniture and fire doors, and check the HMO licence for five or more sharers.
1960s homes in Skelmersdale: photograph flat roofs, older windows and communal footpaths, garages and bin areas.
Victorian terraces in Ormskirk and Burscough: check rear yards, sash or replacement windows and any damp in back kitchens.
Rural homes on the mossland farms: record oil tanks, septic tanks and any signs of subsidence or cracking on soft ground.
New-build estates in Burscough: check sealant, flooring and any snagging marks, and who maintains shared green space.
Stone cottages in Parbold and Up Holland: photograph damp patches, chimneys and timber windows.
tenantHelp: West Lancashire Borough Council's Private Sector Housing team advises private tenants and takes action on disrepair and unsafe conditions.
